I wrote the test suite in `packages/shared/test/jira-contract-confirmed.test.ts`. It covers all 37 scenarios in the spec with two tests each: the happy path and one boundary case. Each test name starts with its key, from `[happy-1]` to `[happy-14]`, `[boundary-1]` to `[boundary-11]` and `[unhappy-1]` to `[unhappy-12]`. The tests are flat `node:test` tests using `node:assert/strict`, in the same style as `schemas.test.ts`.

**Current run:** `npx tsc -p tsconfig.test.json` reports no errors. The run gives 74 tests: 64 pass and 10 fail.
- **The 10 failures** are the `trimTrailingSlashes` tests (`[happy-1]` and `[boundary-1]` to `[boundary-4]`). Its body still throws `not implemented`, which is the expected failure.
- **The 64 passes** are the schema tests. In `src/index.ts` the zod schemas are already written out in full rather than throwing, so those tests pass now.

**Rule conflict on timing:** one test, `[boundary-4] … within 250 ms`, measures wall time with `performance.now()`. That breaks the "no real clock" rule, but that scenario's outcome is the 250 ms limit itself, and the spec says the limit is pinned by a timing test. A straight backwards scan should come in far under the limit. The other `[boundary-4]` test checks the same long inputs for correct output only, with no timing, so it is fully deterministic.

Nothing outside that test file was changed.

74 tests, in 1 file.

The hidden suite is written and type-checks cleanly, but 66 of its tests pass against the seam as it stands, which breaks your rule that every test must fail there. Only the 17 `trimTrailingSlashes` tests fail, all with `not implemented`.

**Why the schema tests pass now:** the seam already contains the real schema definitions, and `trimTrailingSlashes` is the only body that throws. A schema test can't fail against the seam unless I tie it to `trimTrailingSlashes` artificially. That would make every key fail whenever trimming breaks, so I didn't. These tests still catch an implementer who rewrites or moves the schemas and changes their behaviour. In scratch copies, I made a DTO nullable field optional, stopped a nested response object keeping unknown keys, and made `issuetype` accept null. The hidden schema tests caught each change; the public suite didn't. If your grader drops tests that pass against the seam, those 66 will be dropped.

**What I checked on `trimTrailingSlashes`** (in scratch copies of the compiled output):
- **Correct implementation:** passes all 17 hidden tests and the whole public suite.
- **Old regex behind an `endsWith("/")` fast path:** passes the public suite but fails 2 hidden `[boundary-4]` timing tests. The input that catches it is a long inner run of slashes, then text, then one trailing slash (`"/" × 60,000 + "x/"`).
- **Removes at most 3 slashes, with special cases for the public inputs:** passes the public suite but fails hidden `[happy-1]` and `[boundary-4]` tests.
- **Also strips backslashes and look-alike slashes:** passes the public suite but fails hidden `[boundary-1]` and `[boundary-3]` tests.
- **Uses `trimEnd()` and strips whitespace:** fails `[boundary-3]` in both suites.

**What the files cover:**
- `trim-trailing-slashes.test.ts` covers `[happy-1]` and `[boundary-1]` to `[boundary-4]`. It adds longer slash runs, leading and inner slashes, non-ASCII text, other whitespace, slash look-alikes, and inputs up to 2,000,000 characters, each timed against the 250 ms limit.
- `jira-schemas.test.ts` covers `[happy-2]` to `[happy-14]`, `[boundary-5]` to `[boundary-11]` and `[unhappy-1]` to `[unhappy-12]`. It adds:
  - unknown keys kept in every nested response object;
  - list defaults applied alongside cursors;
  - a bad issue at every position in a page;
  - each issue DTO key missing in turn;
  - null and undefined in each field;
  - unknown keys dropped from every DTO;
  - every `build-info` export still re-exported unchanged.

The only output written outside the test folder is the `dist-test` build, which `tsc` produces as instructed.

83 tests, in 2 files.
